chapter: Pianists, Basie, Lil Armstrong and closing
title: Art Tatum's morning sessions at LaRue's
summary: Tatum came every morning after the Three Deuces to LaRue's tavern and played for nine months while drinking beer.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: And then, we had a place at 55th and -- between King Drive and Prairie. And it was a little tavern in the back of a drugstore there at 55th Street called LaRue's. And they had a guy in there, he was supposed to be the manager, they called him Lovey Taylor. And he used to be one of the -- Lovey Taylor used to be a dancer at one time in show business.
Yeah, right, and he -- loudmouth, great big cigar in his mouth, kept his hat on all the time.

This type of a guy, and LaRue was a good guy, and he catered to the musicians, a lot of musicians. And Art would come in there every morning after he got out from work, just as dutifully like he was coming to work, after he got off from the Three Deuces.
And we would sit there until 8:00, 9:00 and 10:00 in the morning, listening to Art Tatum play. And then, he liked

brewermakers. And he'd have his can of beer and his shot, and he would have -- boy, and then we'd ask him different questions and then he would visualize. Now, this is the way I would want this arranged, but this is when he started playing that 'Tea for Two' thing.
Yeah, that, and then he'd be playing one melody with his right hand and another one with his left hand.

This type of thing, and he would be explaining all of these different things to us. And, oh, he just -- I guess that went on for about nine months. Yeah, about nine -- almost every morning, Art Tatum, he'd go over there and we'd hear him play.
So he had his little thing, and then Earl was -- well, he was on the radio from the Grand Terrace and all of that at that time with his band. Yeah.
Well, I also heard that Art would drink all day and all night, and it would never affect his playing.
